title: U.S. history and government
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Trace U.S. history from colonial foundations to the present and explain the Constitution, federalism, the branches and courts, rights, elections and civic participation.

weeks.3: Expansion, slavery and the Civil War
weeks.5: The Progressive Era and World War I
weeks.6: The Great Depression and the New Deal
weeks.11: The three branches and the courts

blocks.deliverable: Explain federalism and the separation of powers with examples.
Analyze the causes of the Civil War from primary sources.
Explain how Progressive reforms changed food and drug safety.
Week 7 midterm; explain the home front and the postwar order.
Analyze a civil rights document and its effects.
Trace a bill through Congress and explain judicial review.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Document-based essay on a historical constitutional question, using five primary sources and presenting the main arguments on each side fairly.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
